correctness.rationale: Shimada's six explicit permutations generate a group of order \(51840\). Exhaustive exact enumeration gives stabilizer orders \(120,240,120,120\), full induced \(\mathfrak S_5\) images in every case, and pointwise-kernel orders \(1,2,1,1\). In the exceptional \(S_2\) case the kernel generator is exactly \(\sigma_6\), it is central, the commutator subgroup has order \(60\), and an explicit involution generates with it a disjoint order-\(120\) complement. These checks prove the claimed direct product rather than only its order.

value.rationale: The isotropy group is the natural stacky/monodromy invariant of a deformation orbit. Shimada's five-line partners have identical incidence combinatorics but orbit degrees differing by a factor of two; the classification identifies the structural reason: only \(S_2\) carries a hidden central Weyl symmetry fixing every marked line. Completing the isotropy classification for both Zariski pairs is more informative than recomputing orbit sizes and exposes a symmetry invisible to the arrangement graph.
